title: Jeju Island 3-Day Itinerary: West Coast, Udo and Hallasan
intro: Plan three days in Jeju, from the turquoise west coast to Sunrise Peak and the south shore. Get a practical route, transport advice, and simple alternatives for rain, wind, or a mountain hike.

overview.note: One side of the island each day

east.note: Start early on the east coast

daythree.note: Choose the mountain or the south coast

segments.voice: Jeju’s black-rock coast opens onto water so clear it looks turquoise.
At Sunrise Peak, a volcanic crater rises straight from the sea.
On Udo, quiet coastal roads invite you to slow down and explore.
And on the south coast, waterfalls tumble into a very different landscape.
By the end, you’ll have the three-day route in order, plus practical options for getting around and changing weather.
Here is the island at a glance: west coast, east coast, then the mountain or the south.
Three days in Jeju, planned plainly.
A little planning makes this route much easier. Jeju is bigger than it looks, so think about your transport, your base, and the day’s weather before you set off.

card.title: A few useful things to know
card.sub: Plan for distance, wind and changing conditions

segments.voice: For a short trip, Jeju City is a practical base. It is close to the airport, and many restaurants and buses start there. Aewol on the west or Seogwipo on the south are alternatives if you want to stay by the coast.

list.heading: Places to base yourself
items: Jeju City: airport, restaurants and buses

segments.voice: If you plan to rent a car, bring your passport and an International Driving Permit, or the type of licence Korea accepts from your country. Check the requirements before you travel.

list.heading: For a rental car
items: International Driving Permit or accepted licence

segments.voice: Book flights from Seoul early for weekends and holidays. This is one of the busiest air routes in the world, so leaving flights until the last moment can make your plans harder.

list.heading: Before your flight
items: Book early for weekends and holidays

segments.voice: Jeju weather changes quickly, and wind is common. Pack a windproof layer whatever the season, and check conditions before outdoor plans, especially a mountain hike or a ferry trip.
Day one follows Jeju’s west coast, with a cafe stop, a beach walk, and an indoor or outdoor afternoon.
Start in Aewol, continue to Hyeopjae, then head inland for the afternoon.
Begin with a coastal drive from Jeju City to Aewol. Lava rock borders the shoreline, and cafes look out over the water. Haejigae Cafe is a relaxed place to pause and enjoy the sea view.

Next, take a slow walk at Hyeopjae Beach. The water is clear and turquoise, and Biyangdo sits just offshore. In summer, people come to swim; in other seasons, the sand and coastal path make a lovely walk.

For lunch, head to nearby Hallim. Then choose the afternoon around the weather. Arte Museum Jeju is a large immersive digital art space and a useful indoor plan when rain makes a long outdoor stop less appealing.

list.heading: Rainy-day option
items: Immersive digital art at Arte Museum Jeju

segments.voice: On a clear day, swap the museum for a short climb up an oreum, one of Jeju’s small volcanic cones. You get a different view over the fields and a taste of the island’s volcanic landscape.
Stay on the west coast for sunset. This side of the island faces the evening light, so you can finish the day by the water before driving back to Jeju City.
Day two is an early start on the east coast, with a crater climb, a ferry to Udo, and a walk above the sea.
The route starts at Seongsan, crosses to Udo, then continues to Seopjikoji.

Start early at Seongsan Ilchulbong, also called Sunrise Peak. This huge volcanic crater rises from the sea and is part of Jeju’s UNESCO World Natural Heritage. The steps to the crater rim take about twenty to thirty minutes.

Come for sunrise or early in the morning to avoid tour groups. After your visit, go to nearby Seongsan Port for the ferry to Udo. Check ferry conditions on the day, because bad weather or strong wind can cancel sailings.

list.heading: Before boarding
items: Check the ferry on the day
Wind and bad weather can cancel sailings

segments.voice: Udo is a small island with white-sand beaches, quiet coastal roads, and peanut ice cream. Rent a bicycle, e-bike, or scooter to explore. Take your time here rather than treating the island as just another quick photo stop.

Back on Jeju, walk the clifftop path at Seopjikoji. It is just south of Seongsan, and the views look back toward Sunrise Peak. On the way back toward Jeju City, families and adventure lovers can consider Jeju Leports Land in Jocheon.
For your final day, choose one big plan: a mountain hike or a slower day among the south coast waterfalls and market.

card.title: Mountain or south coast
card.sub: Pick the day that suits you

segments.voice: Hallasan is the mountain option. The south-coast route links Seogwipo’s waterfalls with the Olle Trail and market.

Hallasan is Korea’s highest mountain, at one thousand nine hundred and forty-seven metres. The summit routes, Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa, take most of a day and require an online reservation for the final section. Check the official Hallasan website for current rules.

list.heading: Summit hike
items: Check current rules and cut-off times

segments.voice: If you want a shorter mountain walk, try the Eoseungsaengak trail. It takes about an hour up and down and gives you a taste of Hallasan without committing to a summit hike.
For any mountain walk, start early and bring water and warm layers. Hallasan can be much colder and windier than the coast, so check the weather before you leave and be ready to change plans.
If you choose the south instead, cross to Seogwipo. Jeongbang Falls drops straight into the sea, making it a striking first stop on this coastal day.
Continue to Cheonjiyeon Falls, which is lit in the evening. Then walk a section of the Jeju Olle Trail along the coast before heading into town for a relaxed finish.

Finish at Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market for snacks and Jeju tangerines. If your visit falls on the second or seventh, twelfth, seventeenth, twenty-second, or twenty-seventh of the month, Jeju City’s Traditional Five-Day Market is another option before you fly home.

list.heading: Market choices
items: Jeju Traditional Five-Day Market on dates ending in two or seven

segments.voice: A car makes this three-day plan much easier, because Jeju’s sights are spread across a large island.

card.title: Around Jeju
card.sub: Choose transport to fit your days

segments.voice: Most visitors rent a car. You will need an International Driving Permit, or the kind of licence Korea accepts from your country, and your passport. Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for driving directions and routes.

You can also reach every stop by bus, but journeys take much longer. If you rely on buses, drop one stop per day and check routes before leaving. Buses may run only every half hour or less often, and timetables can change.
For the east coast, a taxi or day tour can be a useful alternative to driving. Keep the day flexible around the Udo ferry, since wind or bad weather can disrupt the crossing.
These are the common ways to make a short Jeju trip harder than it needs to be.

card.title: Four easy mistakes
card.sub: Leave room for distance and changing conditions

segments.voice: The main things to watch are trying to fit in too much, relying on unplanned bus trips, assuming ferries always sail, and treating Hallasan like a warm coastal walk.

list.heading: Watch out for
items: Too many stops in one day

segments.voice: First, do not plan the whole island in a single day. This itinerary works because it gives the west, east, and south or mountain their own days. If you are travelling by bus, cut a stop rather than racing between sights.

Second, check your bus route and times before setting off. Buses reach the main stops, but they are slower than driving, and some come only every half hour or less often. Timetables can change, so check again before each journey.
Third, do not assume the Udo ferry will run in every kind of weather. Strong wind or bad conditions can cancel it. Check on the day, and keep enough flexibility to adjust your east-coast plan.

And do not underestimate Hallasan. It is colder and windier than the coast. Summit routes also have reservation requirements and strict cut-off times for starting the final climb, so check the rules and weather rather than simply showing up.

list.heading: Before a summit hike
items: Check weather and bring warm layers

segments.voice: Is three days enough for Jeju? It is enough for the west coast, the east coast, and either Hallasan or the south coast. With four or five days, you can slow down, add beaches and oreum, and keep a spare day for rain or a cancelled ferry.

Do you need a car? It makes the trip much easier, but it is not essential. Buses reach the main sights; just plan fewer stops, allow more time, and check current routes and times on Naver Map or KakaoMap.

list.heading: Without a car
items: Use buses, a taxi or a day tour

segments.voice: Do you need to book Hallasan? Yes, for the final summit sections on the Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trails. Shorter trails do not need a reservation. Check the official Hallasan website because rules can change.

label.title: Do I need to book Hallasan?

segments.voice: Keep the plan simple: spend day one on the west coast, day two around Seongsan and Udo, then choose Hallasan or Seogwipo for day three. Check weather, ferry conditions, routes, and current rules before setting out.

list.heading: Three days, one island
items: Day one: Aewol, Hyeopjae and a west-coast sunset
Day two: Sunrise Peak, Udo and Seopjikoji
